Together, Bosco Base (Belgium), Maricuir (Spain), Salesianische Jugendbewegung Österreich (Austria). The aim of this international activity was very clear from the beginning, creating a space where the background of our organisations would feel identified, but also challenged, creating then a conversation that explores the relationship between identity- queer communities- and faith. Through this mobility of youth workers, we aim to equip professionals with practical tools, methods, and soft skills that foster understanding and empathy among people from diverse faith traditions and LGBTQI+ backgrounds. The programme emphasises dialogue-based learning, active listening, and conflict-sensitive communication to help youth workers facilitate inclusive conversations within their own communities. An essential component of this initiative is bringing together youth workers who are engaged in faith-based organisations with those who are not, ensuring a broad spectrum of perspectives. By doing so, we strive to create an open, respectful, and safe space where participants can share experiences, explore challenges, and learn how to support young people who may be navigating tensions between their faith and their sexual or gender identity. Participant profile Youth workers, educators, mentors and community leaders from diverse faith traditions and LGBTQIA+ contexts. Participants should have direct experience working with young people and motivation to apply the tools in their organisations. There is no age limit for this Training Course, but everyone must be +18. Only residents of EU Member States and Third Countries associated with the Programme are eligible to participate. VERTICAL VOICES is a practical Erasmus+ training course for youth workers who want to use storytelling, smartphones and short-form vertical video as tools for participation, self-expression and non-formal learning. This is not a week of PowerPoints. Participants will learn primarily by doing: developing stories, filming, editing, experimenting, giving feedback, facilitating activities and reflecting on how the methods can be transferred into their own work with young people. During the training, we will explore: • storytelling as a tool for youth work • finding and structuring meaningful stories • smartphone filming and visual storytelling • creating short vertical video content with accessible tools • basic editing and practical content-production workflows • facilitation methods that can be used with young people • inclusion and participation of young people with fewer opportunities • consent, privacy, safeguarding and responsible publishing • peer feedback, reflection and adaptation of methods to different youth-work contexts The methodology is based on non-formal education, learning by doing, experiential learning, storytelling laboratories, small-group work, peer feedback, practical creation tasks and reflection. The training is primarily aimed at youth workers, youth leaders, trainers, facilitators, youth project managers, NGO staff and active volunteers who work directly with young people in non-formal learning settings. Participants should be 18+, able to work in English and motivated to apply the methods after returning home. Previous professional filmmaking experience is not required. items.description_text: What happens when we give young people more ways to tell their story? STORY2SPEAK is a practical Erasmus+ training course for youth workers, educators, trainers and facilitators who want to use creative autobiography and storytelling as tools for identity, self-expression, connection and participation. Not every young person finds it easy to explain what they feel, where they belong or what they have experienced. Sometimes conversation alone is not enough. A photograph, fictional character, movement, memory, voice recording or a few written lines can open a different door. During the training, participants will experiment with: • creative autobiography and personal storytelling • creative writing • autobiographical theatre and movement • Photovoice and visual storytelling • Digital Storytelling • identity, voice and self-expression • emotional literacy and reflective practice • consent, boundaries and ethical storytelling • trauma-aware and inclusive facilitation • peer learning and intercultural exchange • adapting creative methods to everyday youth work The training is based on non-formal education and learning by doing. Participants will write, photograph, move, create, experiment, work in groups, reflect and exchange practice. This is not a lecture-based training. Because personal stories can involve sensitive material, particular attention will be given to consent, boundaries, emotional safety and ethical facilitation. Participants always decide how deeply they want to engage with their own personal material. The aim is not to turn participants into artists. The aim is to provide practical creative methods that youth workers can adapt and use with young people in their own organisations and communities. The training is primarily aimed at youth workers, youth leaders, trainers, educators, mentors and volunteers who work directly with young people or communities in non-formal learning settings. items.title: Common Ground: Linking Ecology and Peacebuilding
items.summary: We aim to equip 32 youth workers with tools to connect ecology and peacebuilding, addressing climate change, conflict and social cohesion while strengthening peaceful, sustainable communities.

items.description_text: More info about the training: https://youthpeaceambassadors.medium.com/call-for-participants-common-ground-linking-ecology-and-peacebuilding-5743ecf030ed?sharedUserId=youthpeaceambassadors Common Ground brings together people who want to explore the connection between ecology and peacebuilding. Together, we will look at how environmental issues can contribute to conflict, but also how nature, cooperation, and shared resources can become powerful spaces for dialogue, connection, and peace. Through non-formal education, experiential learning, creative methods, and time in nature, we will explore practical tools that youth workers can use to engage young people with environmental peacebuilding, conflict transformation, and collective action. What you will take away from this: To build participants understanding of the interlinkages between ecology, climate change, and peacebuilding, exploring how environmental issues fuel conflict and how peacebuilding approaches can promote ecological justice. To equip participants with practical tools and methods for eco-peacebuilding, including conflict transformation in environmental disputes, eco-anxiety support, and community resilience practices. To strengthen participant’s competences in facilitating dialogue and cooperation across divides (generational, cultural, political) in the context of ecological challenges and sustainability transitions. To foster creative and community-based approaches for promoting a culture of peace through ecological action, such as storytelling, artivism, conflict transformation, and participatory futures thinking. To support participants in designing at least 5 local eco-peacebuilding initiatives in their communities. To strengthen international cooperation among youth workers, building networks, exchanging good practices, and fostering collaboration for future European eco-peacebuilding initiatives.

items.description_text: InnovatorsLab: Gen Z's Game-Based Peace Building is a transformative initiative empowering Generation Z to lead peacebuilding efforts through creativity, technology, and play. Backed by the Erasmus+ Programme, our cross-border project unites organizations from Bulgaria, Romania, Turkey, Georgia, and Armenia to co-develop groundbreaking methods in conflict transformation. Our mission is to create interactive, gamified, and impactful educational tools that resonate with their needs while building a culture of peace. KEY ELEMENTS: 1. Participants will be introduced to the main outputs, including the educational modules, toolkit, and resources developed throughout the project. 2. Peace Escape Room Demonstration - A live demonstration of the Peace Escape Room created during the project. Young people will participate in the activity while facilitators explain its educational objectives, methodology, and learning outcomes. 3. Panel Discussion: Innovation in Peacebuilding - Interactive discussion with youth workers, educators, and stakeholders on the role of game-based learning and innovative approaches in promoting peace, dialogue, and social cohesion. 4. Working Groups and Future Recommendations - Participants will work in small groups to explore how the project's methodologies, share tools and best practices that can be applied in local communities and organisations. Key recommendations and ideas for future cooperation will be collected and presented. 5. A total of 28 youth workers from different countries will participate in this professional development activity. Participants will have diverse professional backgrounds, including social work, psychology, family services, education, youth work, communication and non-formal education. The project also places a strong emphasis on the meaningful representation and active participation of people with fewer opportunities throughout the entire learning process. Through empathy mapping, role-playing, group work, problem-solving activities, scenario-based exercises and project-based learning, participants will explore empathy, mental health first aid, interpersonal communication and general approaches to promoting psychological well-being. Intercultural learning will be an important component of the project. items.description_text: Arts of Prevention brings together 27 youth workers, project coordinators and artists who share an interest in creative approaches to primary prevention. We will explore how expressive arts, storytelling and creative expression can help young people talk about risky behaviour, unhealthy relationships, digital risks and gender stereotypes. The programme mixes hands-on creative workshops, inputs from experts, peer learning and time to plan future projects together. There will be some lectures, but most of the time you will be active, trying things out and working with others. We also focus on equal opportunities in artistic communities, such as dancers, actors and circus performers, who often face pressure around body image and gender roles. And we want to share simple, accessible approaches that reach young people with fewer opportunities, including young people from rural areas, disadvantaged backgrounds and the LGBT+ community. The main goal is to meet the right people, build trust and start new partnerships and Erasmus+ projects. You will leave with new contacts, concrete ideas for cooperation and a set of creative prevention methods you can use in your everyday work.

items.description_text: The BICYCLE Final Study Visit in Brussels will bring together young people and youth workers from the six project countries: Belgium, France, Italy, Poland, Portugal and Spain. It will take place from 21 to 24 October 2026 and will be the final international activity of the project. The visit will be a chance to discover and share the results, experiences and local initiatives developed throughout the BICYCLE project, which uses cycling and sustainable mobility as tools to strengthen youth participation and civic engagement. During the activity, participants will take part in workshops, discussions, institutional visits and meetings with European stakeholders. They will learn more about how EU institutions work, discuss cycling and sustainable mobility policies, and explore how young people can participate in decision-making processes. The programme will include exchanges with representatives linked to European mobility and transport policies, including DG MOVE. Participants will also develop their advocacy and civic participation skills, present ideas and project outcomes, and exchange good practices with people from the other partner countries. As the closing activity of BICYCLE, the Study Visit will be both a moment to look back at what has been achieved and an opportunity to create new connections and future cooperation between young people, youth workers and policymakers.

items.description_text: About the project Many young people spend increasing amounts of time indoors and online, while nature can be a vital source of connection, well-being and resilience. This training helps youth workers experience nature as an active part of the learning process, not just a backdrop. Participants slow down, observe, and explore their own relationship with nature — then critically reflect on what place nature holds in their youth work now, and could hold in the future. Aim & objectives The training supports youth workers in integrating nature-based learning and eco-friendly practices into their everyday work, strengthening competences in facilitation, activity design, reflection, and translating insights into practice. It follows five steps: Connect (building a safe foundation with self, others and nature), Experience (exploring nature-based methods for well-being and resilience), Critically explore (examining personal nature values and their role in practice), Design (creating activities using a practical template), and Take action (developing a concrete plan for their own work and organisation). Learning approach The training is based on Nature-Based Learning (NBL): learning in, from and about nature, spending as much time outdoors as possible. Through experiential learning — slowing down, observing, and harvesting insights — participants connect experience to practice and move toward concrete action. Central to the approach is a reciprocal relationship with nature: learning from it while exploring how this connection inspires care and responsibility.

items.description_text: ABOUT THE TRAINING COURSE What if you could turn complex ideas into something visual, simple and engaging? Facilitate Visually is a training course focused on graphic facilitation, graphic recording and visual methods in education. Throughout the week, participants will explore practical tools and techniques to use drawings, symbols, visual structures and creative methods to communicate ideas and information in a clearer and more engaging way. The main goal is not to become a professional artist. It is to discover how visual thinking can improve the way we facilitate groups, share information and create educational experiences. The training will give participants the opportunity to practice these methods and develop the confidence to incorporate them into their own educational and youth work activities. items.description_text: The training course “Green Future: Developing young people’s green competences based on the GreenComp Framework” provides an opportunity for youth workers, educators, youth leaders and volunteers to strengthen their competences for integrating environmental sustainability into everyday youth work. Climate change, environmental degradation and the transition towards more sustainable ways of living increasingly influence the lives and futures of young people. At the same time, many youth workers are interested in addressing these topics but do not always have practical methodologies, structured frameworks or sufficient confidence to transform sustainability concepts into engaging non-formal education activities. The Green Future project responds to this need by introducing participants to GreenComp - the European Sustainability Competence Framework and exploring how it can be practically applied in youth work. The training course will gather youth workers from Austria, Croatia, Germany, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro and create an international learning environment where participants can exchange experiences, explore different local realities and jointly develop approaches for sustainability education. Throughout the training, participants will explore the four main competence areas of GreenComp: Embodying sustainability values: understanding and reflecting on sustainability values, fairness and the importance of protecting nature; Embracing complexity in sustainability: exploring interconnected environmental and social challenges, systems thinking and critical thinking; Envisioning sustainable futures: developing the capacity to imagine alternative futures, adapt to change and explore possible sustainable scenarios; Acting for sustainability: strengthening individual and collective capacity to take initiative and contribute to positive environmental and social change. This conference offers an interactive, participant-driven, and practical learning space to explore how digital tools and artificial intelligence can be used responsibly to reinforce youth voices, streamline youth council management, and foster democratic innovation at the local level. Through a mix of plenary sessions, parallel workshops, study visit, and networking spaces, participants will analyze different local youth council models, reflect on local youth engagement, explore digital solutions including AI and co-create future strategies. items.description_text: The Edge Within is an Erasmus+ Training Course for youth workers, trainers, facilitators, educators, community leaders and others actively involved — professionally or voluntarily — in youth work and non-formal learning. Many of us support young people in navigating change, uncertainty, relationships and questions of identity — while meeting similar edges within ourselves. The Edge Within is an invitation to turn some of that attention inward. For one week, 25 participants from Czechia, Latvia, Romania, Italy and Estonia will step away from their everyday routines and gather at an old Scout base surrounded by forests in Nejdek, Czech Republic. Together, we will explore the “edges” within ourselves: our patterns, reactions, boundaries, strengths and the places where we meet uncertainty, discomfort or the not-yet-known. And we will ask how greater awareness of these processes can influence the way we listen, facilitate, hold space and accompany young people. The training combines personal exploration with professional reflection. Through experiential and non-formal learning, nature-based and embodied practices, storytelling, creative expression, movement, reflection, peer learning and community living, participants will first experience the methods themselves — and then explore how they can be meaningfully and ethically adapted to their own youth work. We are looking for people who are curious, open to reflection and willing to participate fully in an experiential learning process. You do not need to be an experienced trainer or have previous experience with nature-based approaches. The setting itself will be part of the journey. We will live simply and closely together, spend meaningful time outdoors and experience November in the Czech countryside as it comes. items.description_text: What if conflict wasn’t a problem to solve, but a language to understand? This project invites you to decode the hidden messages within tension and disagreement, finding paths that lead not just to resolution, but to transformation. By engaging with the roots of conflict and exploring its role in our lives and communities, we’ll explore how it can be a catalyst for creativity, growth, and resilience. This isn’t about avoiding difficulty, it’s about diving into it and reimagining the possibilities on the other side. In a world marked by growing complexity, the need for conflict transformation has never been more urgent. This project invites participants to take a step back, return to the fundamentals, and rediscover the power of dialogue and understanding. Are you ready to shape a new narrative? Aim: To equip 25 youth workers, youth leaders and activists with tools to transform conflicts into opportunities for dialogue and growth, fostering collaboration and building inclusive communities capable of addressing challenges. items.summary: The webinars explore youth well-being through Body, Mind, Emotions and Connection, combining practical tools, experiential activities and approaches such as Nonviolent Communication, embodiment, mindfulness and creative methods.

items.description_text: Wellness Navigators Webinar Series Wellness Navigators is a series of six free online webinars created for youth workers, educators, trainers, facilitators, and anyone interested in supporting the emotional and social well-being of young people. Running from September 2026 to February 2027, the series explores practical approaches to well-being through the four dimensions of the Wellness Compass: Body, Mind, Emotions, and Connection. Each webinar combines accessible theory with practical tools, reflection, and experiential activities that can be used both for personal development and in educational work with young people. Topics include emotional awareness and regulation, connection and empathy, body-based practices, play and joy, and everyday strategies for strengthening resilience and well-being. The webinars are part of the Wellness Navigators Erasmus+ project, which develops practical educational resources to help young people better recognise their needs, understand their emotional and bodily signals, build healthier relationships, and navigate everyday challenges with greater awareness and choice. What to expect Participants will: discover practical tools for supporting youth well-being; explore the connection between body, thoughts, emotions, and relationships; learn experiential activities that can be adapted to youth work and non-formal education; gain inspiration from approaches such as Nonviolent Communication, embodiment, mindfulness, creative methods, and emotional education; receive access to webinar recordings and additional project resources. The webinars are free of charge and open to an international audience. Participants can register once for the whole six-part series and receive information and access links before each session. The webinar series accompanies the development of the Wellness Navigators toolkit and card deck, offering an opportunity to explore some of the ideas and practices behind the resources in greater depth. items.description_text: Context In the first year of our accreditation, "The Outdoor Youth Work" taught us to use outdoor spaces for non-formal learning. Even outside, we met the same obstacle: attention. In discussions with partners during 2026, youth workers named three difficulties: agreeing on phone use without conflict, bringing a distracted group back to an activity, and responding when young people rely on AI for advice. In the wider context, problematic social media use among adolescents rose from 7% (2018) to 11% (2022) across 44 countries (WHO/HBSC, 2024), and 63.8% of 16-24-year-olds in the EU used generative AI tools in 2025 (Eurostat, 2026). AI gives rapid responses. It can support learning, and it may also encourage distraction, reliance on quick answers or less independent thinking. These effects differ between people and tasks, so youth workers need to observe them in themselves first. The outdoors is our deliberate low-tech contrast: away from notifications and feeds, participants can notice their own habits. Goal To enable youth workers to understand how using AI affects their own attention, critical thinking, confidence and decision-making, and to facilitate activities that help young people stay attentive and make intentional choices about technology. Objectives O1. To increase the self-awareness of 20 youth workers (volunteers, aspiring and active practitioners) regarding how AI use affects their own attention, critical thinking, confidence and decision-making, so that each can distinguish situations where AI supports learning from those where it hinders it. O2. To strengthen the competence of the 20 youth workers to facilitate inclusive, well-debriefed activities on attention and to make reasoned decisions on whether AI serves an activity's learning purpose. items.description_text: The overall goal of this training course is to provide youth workers with an opportunity to explore and deepen their understanding of emotional intelligence and its vital role in fostering both individual and collective resilience. Resilience is not about coping alone—it grows through emotional intelligence, relationships, participation and belonging. In times of uncertainty, crisis, and prolonged stress, many young people (as well as adults), develop misconceptions about mental strength. They may believe that suppressing emotions, hiding vulnerability, or coping with everything alone are signs of resilience. Research and life experience consistently show the opposite. Genuine resilience starts within supportive relationships and is built through emotional awareness, healthy self-management, sense of belonging and contribution to something meaningful. Through experiential social and emotional learning (SEL), delivered in synergy with the principles of non-formal education, participants will not only develop these competencies themselves but also experience their practical value in their daily work with young people. The training can be especially valuable for those working with marginalized youth population. The course will further explore how meaningful participation, collaboration and community engagement contribute to individual wellbeing, confidence, and resilience. By strengthening their own emotional intelligence, participants will become better equipped to create safe and empowering environments, build trusting relationships with young people, and support them in developing resilience and becoming active, engaged members of their communities. items.description_text: Humour is already present in youth work practice - but it's rarely used as a deliberate, structured tool. "Humour is Serious Business" (HiSB) is a 6-day Erasmus+ KA153-YOU training course (27 November - 3 December 2026, Hollókő, Hungary) that will help you turn something you probably already do instinctively into an intentional, ethical, and effective competence for engaging young people. This training is aimed specifically at practitioners in the field of non-formal learning and youth work - not at the general public. You should apply if you are a youth worker (professional or voluntary), a youth leader, a young person (18+) with leadership potential already identified by your organisation, or a practitioner with relevant expertise who works with young people (e.g. a coach, mentor or tutor), even if youth work is not your primary profession. Through non-formal methods - World Café, simulations and role play, clowning and improvisation, team building, and daily reflection groups - you will explore the many different types of humour, examine cultural differences in how humour is used, reflect on your own sense of humour, and develop concrete post-programme actions to bring back to your own community. Every participant leaves with a Personal Development Plan and the chance to earn a Youthpass. HiSB is delivered by an experienced international Training Team and hosted by MAVISZ (Hungary), together with partner organisations in Poland, Portugal, Armenia, Serbia, Latvia, Croatia, Montenegro and Spain. 36 participants will take part, 4 per sending country. Full details, including the daily programme, participant support structure, and reimbursement process, are in the Info Pack: https://mavisz.my.canva.site/hisb2026

items.description_text: Overview Are you an aspiring youth worker ready to step up as a facilitator? Join our 7-day Erasmus+ training course designed to equip you with the essential skills, tools, and confidence to design engaging workshops, understand non-formal learning, and kickstart your project organizer journey. Through intensive days filled with practical methods, dynamic activities, and peer exchange, you will explore group dynamics, practice debriefing, and discover how to handle challenging moments in a group. Along the way, we will dive into modern digital tools and AI to support your preparation and project workflow in an effective yet responsible way. You will also get hands-on experience by designing and delivering your own workshop live, receiving feedback from peers and trainers. This training course connects hands-on facilitation to the wider Erasmus+ project lifecycle: from a single 90-minute session to a full international initiative. You will meet motivated peers from across Europe, build lasting partnerships, and realize that your age is not a barrier to becoming a recognized youth worker and facilitator. What You Will Learn Gain insights into creating impactful workshops, particularly within the framework of non-formal education and the Erasmus+ programme. Learn how individual workshops scale into full international youth projects and understand the essentials of project design and project writing. Use digital tools and AI responsibly to boost quality and work more efficiently while learning about potential pitfalls. Develop confidence and practical facilitation competences through live workshop delivery, instruction-giving, and structured debriefing. Build an international network of emerging youth workers from 12 European countries to develop future high-quality Erasmus+ projects together. items.description_text: The European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC) invites youth workers, youth leaders, trainers, community practitioners and other professionals working in non-formal learning and youth work to join the first session of Equal Ground, a quarterly ENRMSC dialogue series exploring meaningful participation, access to opportunities and accountability. About the session A seat at the table means little if the decisions are already made. Equal Ground Q1: Meaningful Participation — Beyond the Seat at the Table explores what meaningful participation looks like when refugees, migrants, stateless people and other communities are not simply invited into conversations, but have genuine opportunities to influence decisions, policies and actions. The session will examine the difference between being present and participating meaningfully. Who gets invited to the table? Who gets heard? Who gets to influence what happens next? Through a participatory, community-centred dialogue, participants will explore barriers to meaningful participation and consider how youth workers, organisations and institutions can create more effective pathways for people with lived experience to contribute to decision-making. What will participants explore? The session will explore: • Meaningful participation beyond consultation and representation • The difference between having a seat at the table and having influence • How lived experience can contribute to knowledge, leadership and decision-making • Barriers that can prevent refugees, migrants, stateless people and other communities from participating meaningfully • The role of youth workers and non-formal learning practitioners in creating inclusive participation • How organisations can listen to communities and translate their perspectives into action • How young people and community changemakers can move from participation to leadership • Practical approaches for creating more inclusive spaces for dialogue and decision-mak

items.summary: Life in It is a two-part Erasmus+ media training for youth workers and educators, combining practical filmmaking, storytelling and short-form video in Germany and Greece, with local practice between the two phases.
items.participants_countries: Czech Republic, Germany, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Poland, Romania, Slovak Republic
items.fee_text: There is a 50 euro participation fee per phase of the project.
items.accommodation_food_text: All accommodation and food costs will be covered by the programme.
items.travel_reimbursement_text: For the travel reimbursement, we follow the Erasmus+ Programme guide and the distance calculator. Please refer to the infopack for the exact amount of your country.
items.description_text: Life in It is a two-part Erasmus+ media training for people active in youth work and non-formal learning, including youth workers, trainers, educators, volunteers, project coordinators and people involved in their organisation’s communication. No previous filmmaking experience is required; the focus is on learning through practice, collaboration and experimentation. The learning journey starts with online preparation and continues with Frame One in Germany (13–19 December 2026), where participants explore practical filmmaking, storytelling and media tools by working in international crews and creating content in real local contexts. Between the two international phases, participants bring the learning into their own organisation or community, including a small focus group with young people and further local practice. The journey continues with Frame Two at Hopeland, Greece (22–29 September 2027), where participants explore how the same storytelling foundations can be adapted to shorter, vertical video and social media formats. The methodology is strongly based on non-formal education and learning by doing: short inputs, practical assignments, teamwork, feedback, reflection and creative decision-making are at the centre of the programme. Life in It is designed as one learning journey rather than two separate trainings, with online preparation, two residential phases, local practice and follow-up. Priority is given to applicants who can take part in the complete process and use the learning afterwards in their youth work, organisation or local community.

items.title: Move, Play, Create : Circus and Physical Theatre as Tools for Youth Work
items.summary: A practical training for youth workers to discover circus and theatre as tools for non-formal education, exploring accessible activities that foster creativity, confidence, cooperation and social connection.

items.description_text: This training course introduces youth workers, educators and facilitators to circus and theatre as practical tools for youth work and non-formal education. No previous circus or theatre experience is required. Through hands-on activities, participants will discover the basics of juggling, partner and group acrobatics, clowning and physical theatre, while learning how to adapt these activities into accessible and meaningful workshops for young people. The course is based on circus pedagogy: an educational approach that uses circus not primarily to train performers, but to support personal and social development. Circus activities create opportunities to cooperate, communicate, build trust, take on challenges, be creative and experience success. Participants will explore how these activities can foster young people's confidence, creativity, cooperation, persistence, coordination and social connection. A key focus will be accessibility and inclusion, exploring how circus can be adapted to different ages, physical abilities, levels of experience and backgrounds. Participants will also discover how a group can move from individual games and activities towards creating a short collective performance. They will explore the pedagogical and practical aspects of the creative process, including generating ideas, sharing roles, connecting different disciplines and ensuring that everyone can contribute. By the end of the training, participants will have a practical repertoire of circus and theatre activities and greater confidence in using them in their youth work.

items.description_text: Project Summary: Leveraging ICT and Social Media for Youth Inclusion and Participation Aim of the Project: The project is designed to equip youth workers with digital skills and tools to strengthen civic participation and engage young people through Information and Communication Technology (ICT). A core aim is to promote civic engagement through digital tools. Objectives: Strengthen Digital Competencies: Provide practical training in ICT, social media engagement, and digital content creation. Youth workers will be trained to guide young people in critical media analysis, recognizing misinformation, and using digital platforms for youth activism and community participation. Ensure Inclusion and Equal Access: Develop strategies to engage marginalized and disadvantaged young people who face barriers to digital participation. Encourage Innovation: Introduce interactive, gamified, and blended learning approaches to make digital engagement more dynamic and adaptive. Strengthen Transnational Cooperation: Establish a European Digital Youth Work Network for collaboration and knowledge exchange, and develop a Digital Civic Engagement Toolkit with practical resources. Outcome: The project aims to significantly enhance the digital skills of youth workers and strengthen youth engagement through the use of digital tools for non-formal education and social participation. It seeks to expand civic participation through youth-led activism and make digital youth work more accessible and inclusive for young people from diverse and disadvantaged backgrounds. The project's sustainability will be ensured through the creation of a European-wide network of digital youth workers and an open-access toolkit, ensuring that the methodologies remain relevant and scalable.

items.description_text: The ENRMSC European Dialogue & Capacity-Building Forum 2027 will take place in Warsaw, Poland, in April 2027. The forum will bring together young refugees, migrants and stateless changemakers, youth workers, youth leaders, researchers, academics, civil society organisations, public institutions and other practitioners working with young people. The forum is built around a simple question: How can we move from young people being affected by systems to young people meaningfully shaping knowledge, opportunities, policies and solutions? The programme will explore meaningful participation, access to education and professional opportunities, community leadership, research and evidence, youth engagement, advocacy and collaboration between communities and institutions. Participants will take part in interactive discussions, panel sessions, workshops and facilitated group activities. The programme will combine knowledge exchange with practical capacity-building and opportunities for participants to develop new connections and potential European cooperation. A particular focus will be placed on recognising lived experience as expertise. Young refugees, migrants and stateless people will not only participate as beneficiaries but as contributors, knowledge holders, community leaders and partners in shaping discussions and recommendations. The forum will also connect participants with relevant European opportunities, networks and potential partners, including opportunities related to youth work, education, research, leadership and civic participation. The event is particularly relevant to people working in non-formal learning and youth work who engage with young people from refugee, migrant and stateless backgrounds. The guiding principle of the forum is: “Nothing About Us Without Us.” The forum is currently being developed by the European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC), a refugee-, migrant- and stateless-led European civil society organisation.

items.description_text: Why this programme? Young people increasingly experience the world through digital, visual, interactive and participatory media. At the same time, heritage education can sometimes remain centred on traditional formats: guided tours, exhibitions, historical information and passive observation. This creates an opportunity for youth work. New media can provide alternative entry points into heritage, allowing young people to: explore places and stories through immersive experiences; discover hidden or forgotten narratives; connect personal and community memories with wider European heritage; question dominant interpretations of history; create their own narratives; collaborate across cultures; transform physical spaces into interactive learning environments. The programme therefore does not aim to turn youth trainers into technology specialists. Instead, it aims to help them become creative facilitators who know when, why and how to use technology to create meaningful learning experiences. General aim To strengthen the capacity of youth trainers to use new media and emerging technologies as tools for heritage awareness, intercultural learning, creativity and youth participation. Design non-formal education activities connecting young people with local, national and European heritage. items.description_text: The project arises from a shared observation among young people, community development professionals, and partner organizations: a growing need to reconnect with the living world, rebuild social bonds, and collectively reflect on current ecological challenges in the face of the climate emergency. It addresses two main needs: Strengthening the skills of facilitators and community leaders so they can design and implement educational projects with strong social and ecological impact. Actively engaging young people in meaningful, concrete, and transformative projects. The project uses the living garden as an educational, sensory, and cooperative tool, helping to recreate connections between humans and ecosystems. These spaces become platforms for social transformation, civic education, and territorial resilience. It is based on active pedagogy that promotes autonomy, local engagement, and the transversal skills required for the ecological transition.
